title: Universal weak schematic density of the jets of a section
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $p:Y\to S$ be a smooth affine morphism of finite presentation with nonempty geometrically connected fibers [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Here geometrically connected means connected after extending each residue field to an algebraic closure. Let $e:S\to Y$ be a section. Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $\epsilon:B\to A$ for its retraction and $J=\ker\epsilon$. For $n\geq0$ set $Y_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J^{n+1})\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $S$-scheme $T$, with no Noetherian or reducedness assumption on $T$, and every closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow Y_T=Y\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product], if each closed immersion $Y_n\times_ST\to Y_T$ factors through $Z$, then $Z=Y_T$ as closed subschemes. In particular the only closed subscheme containing every base-changed $Y_n$ is the whole $Y_T$.

source.place: Conrad, proof of Proposition 2.1.6, printed p.63, universal weak schematic density of the neighborhoods of the section; Definition 2.1.7, p.61, specifies weak schematic density. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this exact assertion.

proof.text: First the fibres of $Y\to S$ are geometrically irreducible. The algebraic-closure criterion [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] turns the stated geometric connectedness into connectedness over every field extension [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], in particular over the residue field itself. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-geometrically-irreducible] to $p,e$: finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Its open $U$ contains every point of the connected component of each fibre through the section. Since each fibre is connected and has its section point, this is the whole fibre; hence $U=Y$. Its geometrically irreducible fibres are therefore those of $Y$.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 2.1.6, proof, printed pp.62--63; affine universal weak density argument. Local copy WANTED; agent expansion using the cited Stacks tools.

proof.text: For an $A$-algebra $C$ put $D_C=B\otimes_A C$ and $J_C=\ker(D_C\to C)$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}D_C$ with $Y_C$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-section-finite-jets], its jet rings are $Q_n\otimes_A C=D_C/J_C^{n+1}$, where $Q_n=B/J^{n+1}$, and each $\operatorname{Spec}Q_n\to S$ is finite locally free. By [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], each $Q_n$ is flat over $A$. The base-changed family $Y_C\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is smooth: [lem-pc-smooth-flat] gives the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change], which gives smoothness near every point; [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] assembles these neighbourhoods. Its fibre at $c$ is the original fibre over the image of $c$, extended to $\kappa(c)$, by associativity of fibre products. Thus step 1 and the definition of geometric irreducibility show that every such fibre is irreducible.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 2.1.6, proof, printed pp.62--63; affine universal weak density argument. Local copy WANTED; agent expansion using the cited Stacks tools.

proof.text: Suppose first that $C$ is Noetherian. The ring $B$ is finitely presented over $A$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to $p$ and the whole affine opens $Y,S$. In particular choose finitely many algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$. The elements $b_i\otimes1$ generate $D_C$ over $C$: express each first factor of a pure tensor as a polynomial in the $b_i$ and use that every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $D_C$ Noetherian. Put $N_C=\bigcap_{n\geq0}J_C^{n+1}$. For every prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq J_C$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-localization] with $R=M=D_C$ and $I=J_C$. Omitting the zeroth power does not change the intersection. It supplies $f_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$ with $(N_C)_{f_{\mathfrak q}}=0$. Thus $V=\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\supseteq J_C}D(f_{\mathfrak q})$ contains the section and every element of $N_C$ restricts to zero on $V$.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 2.1.6, proof, printed pp.62--63; affine universal weak density argument. Local copy WANTED; agent expansion using the cited Stacks tools.

proof.text: Every fibre of $V$ is a nonempty open subset of the irreducible fibre of $Y_C$ (it contains the section point), hence dense: any two nonempty opens of an irreducible space intersect. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] to this open in the smooth family of step 2, taking the identity base change. It says $\mathcal O_{Y_C}\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ is injective. Since every element of $N_C$ vanishes on $V$, injectivity on sections over $Y_C$ gives $N_C=0$. This proves the intersection assertion for every Noetherian $A$-algebra $C$, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 2.1.6, proof, printed pp.62--63; affine universal weak density argument. Local copy WANTED; agent expansion using the cited Stacks tools.

proof.text: Now let $C$ be arbitrary and $b\in\bigcap_nJ_C^{n+1}$. Write $b=\sum_{i=1}^m x_i\otimes c_i$ with $x_i\in B$, $c_i\in C$ and $m\geq0$, using the pure-tensor generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] (the $x_i$ are arbitrary elements of $B$, not the generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of step 3). Let $C_0\subseteq C$ be the subring generated by the image of $A$ and the finitely many $c_i$. It is a finite type $A$-algebra and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Let $b_0=\sum_i x_i\otimes c_i\in D_{C_0}$, which maps to $b$ under $D_{C_0}\to D_C$. For each $n$, the inclusion $C_0\hookrightarrow C$ remains injective after tensoring with the flat $A$-module $Q_n$ of step 2, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. The image of $b_0$ in $Q_n\otimes_A C_0$ maps to zero in $Q_n\otimes_A C$, because $b\in J_C^{n+1}$. Therefore that image was already zero. The quotient identifications from step 2 give $b_0\in J_{C_0}^{n+1}$ for every $n$. Step 4 gives $b_0=0$, hence $b=0$. One fixed $C_0$ works for all $n$; no interchange of infinite intersections and tensor products is used.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 2.1.6, proof, printed pp.62--63; affine universal weak density argument. Local copy WANTED; agent expansion using the cited Stacks tools.

proof.text: Finally cover $T$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}C$. On each such open, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $Y_T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D_C$. The affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] writes $Z$ there as $\operatorname{Spec}(D_C/K)$ for an ideal $K$. The assumed factorization of every jet says that the quotient $D_C\to D_C/J_C^{n+1}$ factors through $D_C/K$, equivalently $K\subseteq J_C^{n+1}$, using [lem-sfb-smooth-section-finite-jets]. Step 5 forces $K=0$. Consequently the ideal sheaf of $Z$ vanishes on this open cover of $Y_T$, hence vanishes globally by the sheaf axiom. Thus $Z=Y_T$ as closed subschemes, including when $T$ is empty.
